brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Strong spatial metaphor with category labels acting as gravitational anchors, suggesting topic proximity rather than rigid hierarchy
Confident dark canvas with restrained accent dots per cluster (amber, pink, teal, violet) creates legible color-coded semantics
Clean sans-serif hierarchy inside cards with consistent meta line (timestamp · pages) reads as a coherent system
dominant_weaknesses: Cards heavily overlap and occlude each other's body text, breaking readability and undermining the spatial-organization premise
Connection lines between related documents are nearly invisible, so the 'topic proximity' claim is asserted but not visually proven
Category labels (RESEARCH, BUSINESS STRATEGY) float at random offsets and get covered by cards, weakening the canvas's structural legibility
fix_priorities: Introduce collision avoidance or z-order/dim-on-hover so overlapping cards don't truncate critical content
Strengthen relational lines with subtle gradients or curvature to make topical clustering visible at a glance
Anchor category labels with clearer territory (soft tinted regions or radial gradients) so clusters feel like places, not noise
Add zoom/pan affordances and a minimap to make the spatial canvas navigable at scale
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective land well thanks to the moody canvas and novel metaphor, but behavioral usability collapses under overlapping unreadable cards.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually nails the spatial-canvas brief, but execution undermines proximity-as-meaning because occlusion and faint links prevent the user from actually reading the topology.
